articles.title: Mckenna Grace Says Refusal to Do Nudity on Camera Is ‘Unrelated’ to Her Disney Princess Dreams
articles.summary: "Silly that it’s become such a source of conversation," the "Sunrise on the Reaping" actress says of her viral Cosmopolitan interview.
articles.body:
Mckenna Grace appeared to take issue with her viral interview in Cosmopolitan on Tuesday, clarifying on Instagram that her quote about dreaming of being a Disney princess and refusing to do on-camera nudity are "unrelated."

"The two quotes being used right now in these titles are unrelated," the "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" star wrote in an Instagram story alongside a screenshot of Variety's coverage of the Cosmo conversation. (The publication's headline, "Mckenna Grace Rejects 'Nudity or Hypersexual Things' in Acting Roles Because 'My Dream Is to Be a Disney Princess Someday,' was what the actress took issue with.)

"I said at this point in my career I think I'm uncomfortable doing something but I respect everyone who does — and I also have a dream job!" Grace continued. "I'm not uncomfortable doing nude scenes/hypersexual roles simply because 'I want to be a Disney princess,' it's just because of my own personal comfortability I have with that sort of thing right now at this point in my life!"

The 20-year-old actress, who got her start as a child and teen star in projects like "Designated Survivor," "I, Tonya" and "The Haunting of Hill House," emphasized that it's "silly that it's become such a source of conversation! So many more important things to talk about."

The pushback came about Tuesday after outlets like Variety , Deadline and People published stories on her boundaries with nudity as if it had to do with her future aspirations of being a Disney princess. The original quote in full was:

"At this point, I definitely don't do nudity or very hypersexual things. I respect anybody who can, but it's terrifying to me. I don't know if that'll ever change. It's not like I only do wholesome things—my character literally gets gutted by Ghostface in Scream—but my dream is to try and be a Disney princess someday."

Grace is one of the many stars of Lionsgate's latest "Hunger Games" adaptation, pulling double duty as twins Maysilee and Merrilee Donner. The former is a tribute from Panem's District 12.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" hits theaters Nov. 20.

articles.title: Di Ferrero faz carinho em filhote de jumento durante visita ao PI | G1
articles.standfirst: Em vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, vocalista do NX Zero aparece dirigindo, encontra um grupo de animais e brinca com o filhote.
articles.summary: Em vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, vocalista do NX Zero aparece dirigindo, encontra um grupo de animais e brinca com o filhote.
articles.body:
O cantor Di Ferrero, vocalista da banda NX Zero, esteve no Piauí e publicou nas redes sociais um vídeo em que aparece fazendo carinho em um filhote de jumento. Durante o passeio, o artista avista o grupo de animais, interrompe o trajeto e se aproxima de um deles.

Na gravação, Di Ferrero conversa com o filhote e brinca com a possibilidade de levá-lo para casa. “Vamos morar lá em casa. Gostei de você. Você gostou de mim. Eu gostei de você” , diz o cantor enquanto faz carinho no animal.

Antes do encontro, o artista aparece parafraseando um trecho de uma música. Ao final do vídeo, ele se despede e deixa uma mensagem sobre o estado: “Bom dia. Bem-vindo ao Piauí, lugar mágico maravilhoso” .

A última passagem de Di Ferrero pelo estado havia ocorrido em novembro de 2023, quando o NX Zero participou do Festival GiraSol, realizado em Teresina nos dias 10 e 11 daquele mês.

articles.title: Ingressos Festival de Parintins 2027: Veja preços e como comprar | G1
articles.standfirst: Pela primeira vez, a compra e o acesso ao Bumbódromo serão totalmente digitais. Não haverá emissão de ingressos físicos nem troca de vouchers nos escritórios da Amazon Best.
articles.summary: Garanta seu lugar no Festival de Parintins 2027: ingressos custam até R$ 4.800 e a venda para a edição de 60 anos será exclusivamente digital a partir de 28 de novembro.
articles.body:
Bumbódromo de Parintins — Foto: Divulgação/Secom

Os ingressos para o Festival Folclórico de Parintins 2027 começam a ser vendidos em 28 de novembro, às 9h (horário de Manaus ), exclusivamente pela internet . Os valores chegam a R$ 4.800 para o passaporte que dá acesso às três noites do evento. Confira os preços abaixo.

A venda será feita pela plataforma BaladAPP by Ticketmaster . Cada CPF poderá comprar até dois ingressos , por Pix ou cartão de crédito, com parcelamento em até três vezes sem juros.

Pela primeira vez, a compra e o acesso ao Bumbódromo serão totalmente digitais. Não haverá emissão de ingressos físicos nem troca de vouchers nos escritórios da Amazon Best.

A edição de 2027 será comemorativa pelos 60 anos do Festival e terá uma identidade visual especial, com o tema "Texturas de nossa infância", que acompanha a tradicional disputa entre os bois-bumbás Caprichoso e Garantido.

Os interessados devem criar uma conta na plataforma BaladAPP by Ticketmaster antes da abertura das vendas.

A partir das 9h de 28 de novembro, basta acessar o site da BaladAPP ( selecionar o Festival de Parintins 2027, escolher o setor e a modalidade de ingresso e concluir o pagamento.

A escolha do assento no mapa não garante reserva . O ingresso só estará confirmado após a aprovação do pagamento.

Não haverá venda por telefone, WhatsApp ou presencialmente nos escritórios da Amazon Best.

O público poderá escolher entre duas modalidades:

Passaporte: dá acesso às três noites do Festival, com um ingresso para cada apresentação.

Avulso: permite assistir a apenas uma noite, escolhida no momento da compra.

As duas modalidades estarão disponíveis nos quatro setores, com opções de inteira e meia-entrada.

Passaporte: R$ 4.800 (inteira) | R$ 2.400 (meia);

Avulso: R$ 1.600 (inteira) | R$ 800 (meia).

Passaporte: R$ 4.500 (inteira) | R$ 2.250 (meia);

Avulso: R$ 1.500 (inteira) | R$ 750 (meia).

Passaporte: R$ 3.960 (inteira) | R$ 1.980 (meia);

Avulso: R$ 1.320 (inteira) | R$ 660 (meia).

Passaporte: R$ 3.000 (inteira) | R$ 1.500 (meia);

Avulso: R$ 1.000 (inteira) | R$ 500 (meia).

Sobre o valor total da compra será cobrada uma taxa de processamento de 2%, informada antes da finalização do pagamento. Nenhum setor inclui serviço de open bar.

Os ingressos serão disponibilizados no aplicativo BaladAPP by Ticketmaster após a confirmação da compra. O QR Code será liberado 72 horas antes de cada noite de apresentação .

No dia do Festival, o público deverá abrir o ingresso no aplicativo e apresentar o QR Code junto com um documento oficial com foto.

Não serão aceitos ingressos impressos, capturas de tela ou fotografias do QR Code.

Como indicar outra pessoa para usar o ingresso

Quem comprar ingressos para outras pessoas deverá informar o nome de cada usuário na área "Meus Ingressos", no site da BaladAPP.

A pessoa indicada também precisa ter cadastro na plataforma, com o mesmo e-mail informado na indicação.

O prazo para indicar ou trocar o usuário termina às 16h do dia da apresentação. Será permitida apenas uma troca após a primeira indicação.

No caso do Passaporte, a indicação poderá ser feita separadamente para cada noite.

A meia-entrada será oferecida às categorias previstas na legislação, como estudantes, idosos a partir de 60 anos, jovens de baixa renda inscritos no ID Jovem, professores, profissionais da saúde, doadores regulares de sangue, órgãos e medula óssea e pessoas com deficiência, além de acompanhantes quando previsto em lei.

Para utilizar o benefício, será necessário apresentar documento oficial com foto e comprovante válido da condição que garante o desconto.

Os ingressos específicos para pessoas com deficiência (PCD) serão organizados pelo Governo do Amazonas e não estarão disponíveis na BaladAPP ou na Amazon Best.

As orientações podem ser obtidas pelos seguintes contatos:

Secretaria de Estado de Cultura e Economia Criativa (SEC-AM): (92) 3633-2850 e (92) 3633-3041.

Secretaria de Estado de Justiça, Direitos Humanos e Cidadania (Sejusc-AM): (92) 99324-5933.

O cancelamento poderá ser solicitado pela conta da BaladAPP em até sete dias após a compra, desde que o pedido seja feito com mais de 48 horas de antecedência da apresentação.

Para ingressos avulsos, será considerada a data do evento escolhido. No Passaporte, a referência será a primeira noite, em 25 de junho de 2027.

O prazo de reembolso é de até 72 horas para pagamentos por Pix e de 15 a 60 dias úteis para cartão de crédito. A taxa de processamento de 2% também será devolvida em caso de cancelamento integral da compra.

O não comparecimento ao evento não garante reembolso.

A Amazon Best terá pontos de atendimento em Manaus e Parintins para orientações sobre cadastro e indicação de usuários. Os escritórios não venderão ingressos nem farão reservas ou retiradas.

Manaus: Rua Nova Prata, 225, Nossa Senhora das Graças.

Parintins: Rua Vieira Junior, 754, Centro, em frente ao porto.

O atendimento da BaladAPP também pode ser feito pelo telefone (62) 3434-8450, pelo chat do site e aplicativo ou pelo e-mail contato@baladapp.com.br .

articles.title: 'Jailer 2' box office collection Day 21 [Live]: Rajinikanth's film heads for all-time record for a Tamil film, nears Rs 464 crore net in India
articles.summary: Rajinikanth's 'Jailer 2' is witnessing a gradual slowdown at the domestic box office as it moves further into its third week in theatres.
articles.body: Rajinikanth's 'Jailer 2' is witnessing a gradual slowdown at the domestic box office as it moves further into its third week in theatres. The Nelson Dilipkumar directorial, which opened to strong numbers, continues to attract audiences across Tamil, Telugu and Hindi markets. Even though its collection each day has decreased quite a bit from the opening week, the entertainment film continues to contribute towards its total earnings. The film has already crossed several major box-office milestones and is now inching closer to another domestic collection landmark.'Jailer 2' set for a record milestone'Jailer 2' opened strongly at the box office, collecting Rs 334.35 crore net in its first week across India. The Rajinikanth starrer added another Rs 95.55 crore net in its second week, taking its two-week domestic net collection to Rs 429.90 crore. With its India gross now nearing Rs 543 crore, the film is closing in on becoming the highest-grossing Tamil film of all time, with Vijay's 'LEO' (Rs 223 crore) record in Tamil Nadu also within reach.'Jailer 2' Live box office collectionAccording to Sacnilk, 'Jailer 2' has earned Rs 2.18 crore net in India on Day 21 so far from 6,891 shows. The Tamil version leads with Rs 1.33 crore from 3,048 shows, followed by Hindi with Rs 50 lakh from 3,141 shows and Telugu with Rs 35 lakh from 702 shows. With this, the film's India gross has reached Rs 544.22 crore, while its India net stands at Rs 465.23 crore. These are live estimates, and the final Day 21 numbers are expected later tonight.'Jailer 2' day-wise box office collectionWeek 1: Rs 334.35 croreWeek 2: Rs 95.55 croreDay 15: Rs 4.25 croreDay 16: Rs 2.70 croreDay 17: Rs 3.38 croreDay 18: Rs 11.20 croreDay 19: Rs 3.40 croreDay 20: Rs 3.35 croreDay 21: Rs 2.18 croreTotal India net: Rs 465.23 croreTotal India gross: Rs 544.22 croreDirected by Nelson Dilipkumar, 'Jailer 2' features Rajinikanth as Tiger Muthuvel Pandian. The film also stars Mohanlal, Shivarajkumar, Ramya Krishnan, Vidya Balan, SJ Suryah, Mithun Chakraborty, Jackie Shroff, Yogi Babu and several others in important roles. Anirudh Ravichander has composed the music for the action entertainer, which is backed by Sun Pictures. With its third-week collections slowing down, the film's performance over the coming days will be important in determining how much further it can add to its impressive box-office total.DISCLAIMER: The box office numbers and the data in this article are compiled from public and industry sources. All figures are approximate unless explicitly mentioned, offering a fair representation of the movie's box office performance. These totals may change as official studio data is updated or as additional international market reports are finalized. articles.title: Elizabeth Holmes’ partner, Billy Evans, speaks out following the release of ‘You Can See Everything’
articles.summary: Billy Evans, Elizabeth Holmes’ partner, is sharing his thoughts on “You Can See Everything,” including what he believes is the biggest misconception about him and a slew of other topics.
articles.body: Billy Evans, Elizabeth Holmes’ partner, is sharing his thoughts on “You Can See Everything,” including what he believes is the biggest misconception about him and a slew of other topics. On Nov. 3, Evans invited people to participate in an AMA, ask me anything, on X, prefacing it needed “to be legally permisible (sic).” Among the lightest questions include someone asking what the first thing he and Holmes will do after she is released from prison. “Hold our kids tight and talk all night,” Evans, who shares two children with the Theranos founder replied. Holmes was found guilty of four counts of wire fraud for misrepresenting to investors what her company’s technology could do. She was sentenced to 11 years in prison in 2022 and is currently at a minimum-security prison in Bryan, Texas. “You Can See Everything,” the documentary by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, followed her and Evans weeks before she was incarcerated. The film has become a critical and commercial success, with many viewers and experts questioning her and Evans’ intentions. Fielder had previously shared during a Los Angeles screening in October that Evans had yet to watch the film ahead of its Oct. 16 release. When asked on X what he misses most about Holmes, Evans said “everything.” “I miss her presence. Her touch. The way she runs her fingers through my hair. Her patience. She makes me a better person. And without her, I feel an emptiness that’s hard to describe,” he wrote. “People often say they need someone when what they really mean is that they want them. I’ve thought a lot about that distinction. I need Liz. She should qualify as a medically necessary prescription.” When someone followed up by replying, “Her scrambled eggs,” Evans replied, “Def not this,” with a melting face emoji. In the documentary, there’s a moment when Holmes is whisking eggs in a yellow bowl. As she’s speaking to Fielder, Evans grabs the bowl from her hands and starts to vigorously whip them. When the filmmaker questions his move, Evans implies it’s because his partner doesn’t do it right. On X, Evans also shared he had seen “almost all of” Fielder’s work before filming “You Can See Everything.” He also wrote that they celebrated Fielder’s birthday “around the table in Del Mar with my family,” adding, “He also missed the Time 100 dinner, so we celebrated that too.” TODAY.com has reached out to Evans, Fielder and Holmes for additional comment. He also touched on more serious matters, including the “one misconception from the film” that he would like to dispel. “That I somehow control Liz. Anyone who actually knows her would find that idea hilarious. She’s fiercely independent, strong-willed, and my best friend,” he tweeted. “We are partners in every sense. We challenge each other, disagree, and face the world together. Her closest friends are also some of my closest friends. If I ever mistreated her, they’d have my head.” Someone also wondered why, in the documentary, he stopped Fielder from speaking to Holmes’ father. “Both Nathan and the audience saw it as integral to the documentary to truly ‘see everything,’” the person wrote. “It felt like a missed opportunity that could have continued to give Liz more light.” In his response, Evans noted that Holmes was going to prison and had three days together. “I wanted to spend that time together. He interviewed her parents after she went in. They chose not to include that in the film. I didn’t control the edit. If there was something the directors wanted from them they had multiple opportunities to get it.” When questioned about using his power of attorney over Holmes and going directly to X instead of her for her profile password, he wrote that they “discussed this at length over several months. She knew exactly what we were doing.” “We talk about everything, including X. Nothing happened behind her back,” he claimed. “The POA was simply the legal mechanism that allowed me to act on her behalf while she’s incarcerated. It was not a substitute for her consent.” When pressed for more clarity, he replied that Holmes’ account was “tied to an old Theranos email. Password forgotten.” “You Can See Everything” has continued to be a topic of conversation online. Whether the attention has been good or bad for Evans it’s unknown. However, when asked if he regretted agreeing to the documentary, he simply wrote, “Not at all.”

images.caption: Elizabeth Holmes and Billy Evans during the filming of A24's documentary "You Can See Everything".

articles.title: Eyebrows were raised when Saif Ali Khan, Kareena Kapoor Khan decided to move in together before marriage: 'Since I am from the Kapoor khandaan, but I didn’t see anything wrong in it'
articles.summary: Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor have been married for over 14 years, but their relationship attracted considerable attention even before they tied the
articles.body: Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor have been married for over 14 years, but their relationship attracted considerable attention even before they tied the knot in 2012. The couple had reportedly lived together for nearly five years before getting married, a decision that was considered unconventional at the time. Known as ‘Saifeena’, they often found themselves in the spotlight, with their choice to share a home before marriage becoming a talking point. Over the years, Kareena, Saif and their family members have spoken about how they reacted to the decision. While Kareena's family initially had reservations, Saif's mother, Sharmila Tagore, was particularly struck by the actress's candidness about their live-in relationship.In a 2019 conversation with Humans of Bombay, Kareena looked back at the time she spent with Saif on the sets of 'Tashan', where their relationship began. She spoke about how different they were and the influence he had on her. “He’s 10 years older than me and has two kids. But for me, he was just Saif. He helped me heal and love myself. Maybe it was the fact that we’re so different – he’s more private & not ‘Bollywoodised’, but I imbibed that from him. I learnt to balance things and not let them get to me,” she said.Kareena also recalled how Saif first suggested that they move in together. Having dated for some time, he felt they should spend more time together instead of continuing to drop her home every night. The actor subsequently spoke to Kareena's mother about their plans.“We’d been dating for a while, when he said he’s not 25 and can’t keep dropping me home every night. So he told my mom, ‘I want to spend the rest of my life with her. We want to live together.’ My mom was cool with it. It’s so easy with him. Even when we decided to get married, it felt right,” she recalled.However, the decision did invite some criticism, particularly because Kareena belonged to the illustrious Kapoor family. Her father, Randhir Kapoor, is the son of legendary filmmaker and actor Raj Kapoor, while her great-grandfather, Prithviraj Kapoor, was among the pioneers of Indian cinema. Her extended family includes actors Shashi Kapoor, Shammi Kapoor, Rishi Kapoor and Neetu Kapoor. Her mother Babita and sister Karisma Kapoor have also been part of the film industry, while cousin Ranbir Kapoor is among the leading actors of the current generation.In Gunjan Jain's book 'She Walks She Leads', Kareena spoke about why she decided to move out of her mother's home and share a house with Saif. She acknowledged that the decision surprised some people but maintained that she had nothing to hide.“Saif and I moved in together because I was ready to leave my mother’s house, and if he and I did not live together, we would barely meet. There were some raised eyebrows, especially since I am from the Kapoor khandaan. But I was always honest about it.”She also explained why she did not consider living together before marriage an issue, drawing a comparison with the way relationships are approached in the film industry. “In Bollywood, the tried-and-tested formula always works, so why not try and test a relationship? I didn’t see anything wrong in it.”Her sister Karisma Kapoor admitted that the decision had initially taken her by surprise as well. However, she eventually understood that Kareena was following her instincts and making a choice she believed was right.“It was for me too, to some extent. Our family is slightly conservative but then we accepted that this was Bebo: all heart and all sentiment. Besides, she has this incredible ability to always know what is right for her. She is led by emotion and instinct but, touch wood, her decisions have always proved to be positive and wise,” Karisma said.Karisma had previously shared screen space with Saif in films such as 'Hum Saath-Saath Hain', even before Kareena made her acting debut.Saif's mother, veteran actor Sharmila Tagore, had a rather different experience when she discovered that the couple were living together. During her appearance on 'Koffee with Karan' in 2023, she recalled a gathering at her Delhi home where Kareena casually spoke about her life with Saif in front of several guests.“I had friends over, lots of people from Delhi. These two came and were sitting there. I casually said, ‘What’s happening?’ and she (Kareena) said, ‘When Saif woke up in the morning, he told me this…’ giving the impression that they are living together. This is Delhi and these are my friends of my age,” she recalled.Sharmila, who had herself lived with Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi, fondly known as Tiger Pataudi, before marrying him in 1968, was amused by how openly Kareena spoke about their arrangement. Comparing the two generations, she said:“I was just thinking how the world has changed. When I was living with Tiger, when I was not married, I would not have said to a room full of people that I am living with him. It would have been a deep, dark secret. Maybe everyone would have known, but I wouldn’t have said it. But she said it so naturally that when I even think about it, I sort of laugh at how simple and sorted she is.”Saif Ali Khan and Kareena Kapoor got married in October 2012. They welcomed their first son, Taimur Ali Khan, in December 2016, while their younger son, Jeh Ali Khan, was born in February 2021.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: Actress Mckenna Grace rejects Hollywood nudity, 'hypersexual' roles
articles.summary: Mckenna Grace revealed she won't do nudity or hypersexual scenes in Hollywood, separately saying her ultimate dream is to become a Disney princess someday.
articles.body: Rising Hollywood star Mckenna Grace has drawn a firm line against participating in on-screen nudity, and separately revealed that her dream is to one day play a Disney princess. Speaking with Cosmopolitan, Grace explained that she respects actors who appear in explicit scenes but said those roles do not align with her personal career goals. "At this point, I definitely don’t do nudity or very hypersexual things," Grace said when asked whether there were any roles she would turn down. "I respect anybody who can, but it’s terrifying to me. I don’t know if that’ll ever change," she added. NATALIE PORTMAN SAYS BEING SEXUALIZED AS A CHILD STAR FORCED HER TO BECOME A 'GOOD GIRL' AS PROTECTION The 20-year-old actress, who is set to appear in the upcoming "Hunger Games" prequel "Sunrise on the Reaping," began acting as a child. Her credits include the "Ghostbusters" films, "Scream 7" and Hulu's "The Handmaid’s Tale," for which she earned an Emmy nomination. Grace said she does not intend to limit herself to wholesome roles. However, she hopes to pursue opportunities that align with her personal boundaries and long-term ambitions. "It’s not like I only do wholesome things — my character literally gets gutted by Ghostface in ‘Scream’ but my dream is to try and be a Disney princess someday," Grace added. On Tuesday, Grace clarified on Instagram that "The two quotes being used right now in these titles are unrelated," referring to her comments about wanting to play a Disney princess role. "I’m not uncomfortable doing nude scenes/hypersexual roles simply because ‘I want to be a Disney princess,’ it’s just because of my own personal comfortability I have with that sort of thing right now at this point in my life!" Grace added. DISNEY ALUM CHRISTY CARLSON ROMANO RIPS HOLLYWOOD FOR FAILING CHILD STARS AFTER HAYDEN PANETTIERE’S DEATH Grace is not alone in setting boundaries around intimate scenes in Hollywood. Entertainment critic Christian Toto suggested that Grace’s earlier appearances on family-friendly shows may have influenced her decision. "Mckenna got her showbiz start on family-friendly shows like ‘Crash & Bernstein.’ Perhaps some of those lessons have stuck," Toto, host of "The Hollywood in Toto Podcast," told Fox News Digital. "Or, she's seen former child stars go the hyper-sexual route and wants no part of it. Either way, her instincts here are solid, and she may just carve a healthy lane for her Hollywood career moving forward," he added. Actress Amy Adams previously recalled turning down a sexually explicit comedy sketch after portraying Giselle in Disney’s 2007 film "Enchanted." Speaking on "Late Night with Seth Meyers," Adams said she declined a graphic "Saturday Night Live" musical sketch proposed by Andy Samberg because she was mindful of the film's young audience. "I was so keenly aware of all the young girls that were watching ‘Enchanted,’" Adams said. "And I didn’t want to be the princess singing about that particular act, you know?" BELLA THORNE SAYS HOLLYWOOD TREATED HER LIKE A KID ON SCREEN AND AN ADULT OFF CAMERA Other actors have also established boundaries around intimate scenes. "You" star Penn Badgley discussed his request to reduce intimate scenes on his "Podcrushed" podcast in 2023, citing his marriage as a factor in the decision. Veteran actor Neal McDonough has also spoken publicly about his longstanding refusal to participate in sex scenes or kiss other actresses on screen, citing his Catholic faith and respect for his wife. Meanwhile, Angel Studios announced "The Angel Promise," a set of content standards that the Utah-based studio says will prohibit on-screen sex, nudity and gratuitous profanity in its original releases. In an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, Angel Studios co-founder and chief content officer Jeff Harmon argued that Hollywood has increasingly moved away from the values of family audiences. "I think Hollywood generally kind of lives in a bubble," Harmon said. "These are excellent craftsmen. They're the best storytellers in the world. Hollywood has built the best storytelling infrastructure in the world." COMEDIAN LEANNE MORGAN CALLS OUT HOLLYWOOD FOR LIVING IN A 'BUBBLE' AND MISJUDGING WHAT AUDIENCES WANT TO SEE "But at the same time, they've kind of drifted more and more away from the values-based audience that they used to serve," Harmon said. "And with that, in our view, as brothers and as fathers, as a father, Hollywood hasn't been giving me consistently what I need. Once in a while, you get a good one, but you have to sift through all these things to find your good movies and your good stories." Harmon said that the studio's pledge guarantees families will never have to worry about encountering graphic material, reflecting what he described as an audience-first model that aims to step out of the "Hollywood bubble" and into "middle America's shoes." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Fox News Digital’s Rachel del Guidice contributed to this report.

articles.title: Badshah reviews 'Ramayana' ahead of release, says, 'Every frame is breathtaking' and praises Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi, Yash and the entire cast: 'Jatayu scene is insane'
articles.summary: All eyes are on ‘Ramayana’ as the Nitesh Tiwari directorial arrives in theatres tomorrow, November 5.
articles.body: All eyes are on ‘Ramayana’ as the Nitesh Tiwari directorial arrives in theatres tomorrow, November 5. Ahead of the release, singer and music composer Badshah has watched the film during the special screening which was held in Mumbai and shared a glowing review online, praising its visuals, music and performances.Badshah’s review of ‘Ramayana’Replying to an X post from a user who said they were excited after seeing the rave reviews, Badshah wrote, “You have to watch it. Namit has delivered. Every frame is breathtaking. The characters feel so real. It made me cry, even when we’ve known the story since our childhood. INCREDIBLE BGM. Ranbir, Sai Pallavi, Ravi Dubey, Yash, Lara Dutta, Arun Govil, Rakul. Everyone nailed it. Jatayu scene is insane. And wait for the moment when the dharti amber theme comes. CLAPSSSS. PLEASE GO WATCH IT.”Biggest Indian film in terms of scale‘Ramayana’ is being called the biggest Indian film in terms of scale and budget. Made on a reported budget of Rs 4000 crore, it is among the most expensive productions in the world. The VFX is by eight-time Oscar-winning studio DNEG, and the film is being promoted as India’s answer to Hollywood blockbusters. Sony Pictures is handling the global release, which will reach 70,000 screens, the widest for any Indian film. The film had its world premiere in Los Angeles last week, followed by a special screening in Mumbai on Tuesday for the cast, crew and members of the film fraternity.About ‘Ramayana’Produced by Namit Malhotra’s Prime Focus and Yash’s Monster Mind Creations, the film stars Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana. The star cast also includes Sunny Deol, Ravie Dubey, Anupam Kher, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Adinath Kothare, Arun Govil, Indira Krishnan, and Lara Dutta.Part one releases worldwide on November 5, 2026, while part two is set for 2028. articles.title: Actor assault case: HC reserves verdict on lawyer’s plea seeking contempt action against former judge
articles.summary: Kerala HC reserves verdict on lawyer TB Mini’s plea seeking suo motu contempt against former judge over alleged derogatory remarks in 2017 actor assault trial.
articles.body: Kochi: The high court on Wednesday reserved its judgment on a petition filed by T B Mini, the survivor’s counsel in the 2017 actor assault case, seeking suo motu contempt proceedings against former Ernakulam district judge Honey M Varghese for allegedly making derogatory remarks against her in open court during the trial.While considering the petition, Justice P V Kunhikrishnan orally questioned how the court could expunge remarks allegedly made by the trial court judge if they did not form part of the judicial record. The judge also observed that if the petitioner’s grievances concerned the media coverage, she could approach the Press Council of India.According to Mini, on Jan 12, 2026, the presiding officer of the trial court accused her, while she was representing the survivor, of attending the trial for fewer than 10 days, sleeping in court and treating the courtroom as a “resting place”. She alleged that the remarks, made in the presence of the media, were widely broadcast, triggering online abuse, character assassination and professional defamation against her.Mini had earlier approached the advocate general seeking sanction to initiate contempt proceedings. However, the request was rejected on April 22, 2026, with the observation that the judge’s remarks, even if true, amounted to “excessive or extravagant language” and did not meet the legal threshold for criminal contempt under the Contempt of Courts Act. Challenging the decision, Mini approached the HC, contending that the advocate general’s refusal to grant sanction did not curtail the high court’s inherent constitutional power to take suo motu cognisance of the matter.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kochi | Silver Rate in Kochi | Bank Holidays in Kochi | Public Holidays in KochiStay updated with the latest Kochi news.
